title: Early signs
literal_meaning: Tulasi gives off its fragrance from its first two leaves.
explanation: The small plant provides an image for qualities becoming noticeable early. Someone may use the saying when a beginner already shows promise. Early signs can be encouraging without fixing what a child or learner must become.
meaning_odia: ତୁଳସୀର ଛୋଟ ପତ୍ରରୁ ବାସନା ଜଣାପଡ଼ିବାର ଚିତ୍ରରେ ଆରମ୍ଭରୁ ଗୁଣର ଆଭାସ ମିଳିବା କଥା କୁହାଯାଏ। କାହାର ପ୍ରଥମ ଚେଷ୍ଟାରେ ଦକ୍ଷତା ଦେଖିଲେ ପ୍ରଶଂସାରେ ଏହା କୁହାଯାଇପାରେ। ଆରମ୍ଭର ଆଭାସ ଉତ୍ସାହ ଦେଇପାରେ, କିନ୍ତୁ ସେଥିରୁ ଜଣଙ୍କ ସମ୍ପୂର୍ଣ୍ଣ ଭବିଷ୍ୟତ ନିର୍ଣ୍ଣୟ ହୁଏନାହିଁ।
usage_example: A new student notices a useful pattern in a problem before the lesson has finished. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)

title: Some help rather than none
odia: ନାହିଁ ମାମୁଁ ଠଉଁ କଣା ମାମୁ ଭଲ
literal_meaning: A one-eyed maternal uncle is better than no maternal uncle.
explanation: The comparison expresses a preference for an imperfect resource over having none. Its family image assumes that an uncle can offer care or assistance. The point can be explained without treating disability as a measure of a person’s worth.
meaning_odia: ସବୁ ସୁବିଧା ନଥିଲେ ବି କିଛି ସାହାଯ୍ୟ ମିଳିବା, କିଛି ନମିଳିବାଠାରୁ ଭଲ—ଏହା ଏଠାରେ ମୂଳ ଭାବ। ସୀମିତ ସମ୍ବଳରେ ଉପଯୋଗୀ ବାଟ ବାଛିବା ବେଳେ ଏହି ଅର୍ଥ ଖାପ ଖାଏ। ପୁରୁଣା ଉପମାରେ ଥିବା ଶାରୀରିକ ଅବସ୍ଥାକୁ ମଣିଷର ମୂଲ୍ୟ କମାଇବାର ମାପକ ଭାବେ ନେବା ଉଚିତ ନୁହେଁ।
usage_example: A reading group uses a small borrowed room while waiting for a larger meeting space. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)

title: The same work, even in heaven
odia: ଢିଙ୍କି ସ୍ୱର୍ଗକୁ ଗଲେ ବି ଧାନ କୁଟିବ
literal_meaning: Even if the dhinki goes to heaven, it will still pound paddy.
explanation: The joke gives a rice-pounding implement a grand change of address but leaves its work exactly as before. In conversation, it can tease someone who brings an old habit into a new setting, or express frustration that a change of place has changed nothing. The pointed contrast is between heaven and the same everyday task.
meaning_odia: ଢିଙ୍କିର ଜାଗା ବଦଳିଲା, କିନ୍ତୁ ତାହାର ଧାନ କୁଟିବା କାମ ବଦଳିଲା ନାହିଁ। ପରିବେଶ ବଦଳିଲେ ବି ପୁରୁଣା ଅଭ୍ୟାସ ରହିଯିବାକୁ ଏହି ଚିତ୍ରରେ କୁହାଯାଏ। ମଣିଷର କାମ ବା ଭବିଷ୍ୟତ ଜନ୍ମରୁ ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦିଷ୍ଟ ବୋଲି ନୁହେଁ, ପରିବର୍ତ୍ତନ ସହ ଅଭ୍ୟାସ ବଦଳୁଛି କି ନାହିଁ ସେହି ପ୍ରଶ୍ନ ଏଠାରେ ଉପଯୋଗୀ।
usage_example: On a holiday, a friend immediately starts organising everyone’s timetable just as at work. Another friend uses the saying with a laugh. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: Dhinki is retained as the name of the traditional rice-pounding implement; paddy is rice still in its husk. Heaven supplies the exaggerated destination. This reading does not turn an implement’s fixed function into a claim that people cannot change, or that anyone must remain in an inherited occupation.

title: An impossible demand
literal_meaning: Swear by your father and swallow the dheṅki.
explanation: The image turns coercion into an absurd demand: an oath cannot make an impossible task reasonable. The source gloss concerns forcing someone to act.
meaning_odia: ଶପଥର ଦୋହାଇ ଦେଇ ଢିଙ୍କି ଗିଳିବା ପରି ଅସମ୍ଭବ କାମ କରାଇବାର ଦାବି ହେଉଛି। ଆବେଗ ବା ବାଧ୍ୟବାଧକତା ଦେଖାଇଲେ ଅନୁଚିତ ଦାବି ଉଚିତ ହୋଇଯାଏନାହିଁ। କାହାକୁ କଥା ମାନିବାକୁ ଚାପ ଦିଆଯାଉଛି, କିନ୍ତୁ କାମଟି କରିହେବ କି ନାହିଁ ସେହି ବିଚାର ହରାଇଯାଉଛି।
usage_example: A supervisor demands that a week’s work be completed immediately. (Original editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: Dheṅki is a large husking implement; swallowing it is hyperbole, not an action to imitate.

title: Say what you want in time
odia: ଚଇତା ! ତବତ ଖାଇବୁ କି ପଖାଳ ଖାଇବୁ ବେଳ ଥାଉଁ ଥାଉଁ କହିଥା
literal_meaning: Chaita! Will you eat hot food or pakhala? Say so while there is still time.
explanation: The pointed address and choice between hot food and pakhala turn a practical request into a memorable line: say what you want while another person still has time to arrange it. The dictionary marks Chaita as a non-respectful form of Chaitanya, so the tone can carry impatience or a dismissive edge. Applying it to other decisions is an editorial reading of the complete quoted example; its first occasion is unknown.
meaning_odia: ତବତ ଖାଦ୍ୟ ନା ପଖାଳ—କଣ ଖାଇବ, ତାହା ବେଳ ଥାଉଁ କହିବାକୁ ଚଇତାକୁ କୁହାଯାଉଛି। ଅନ୍ୟ ଜଣେ ବ୍ୟବସ୍ଥା କରିବାକୁ ହେଲେ ଆମ ଇଚ୍ଛାଟି ଆଗରୁ ଜାଣିବା ଦରକାର। ସବୁ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତି ସରିଗଲା ପରେ ମତ ବଦଳାଇବାଠାରୁ ସମୟରେ କହିଦେବା ଭଲ—ଏହି ଦୈନନ୍ଦିନ ବିଚାରଟି ଏଠି ଖାଇବା କଥାରେ ଆସିଛି।
english_summary: A meal cannot be arranged around an answer that arrives too late.
odia_summary: ତବତ ଖାଦ୍ୟ ନା ପଖାଳ—କଣ ଖାଇବ, ତାହା ବେଳ ଥାଉଁ କହିବାକୁ ଚଇତାକୁ କୁହାଯାଉଛି।
usage_example: A friend arranging a shared journey asks everyone to confirm their plans before tickets are booked. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: The source identifies Chaita as a non-respectful or dismissive form of Chaitanya. No particular historical person or household is established. Pakhala remains a named food; the wording should not be softened into a uniformly polite request.

title: Kartika brings a chill at night
explanation: The echo between କାର୍ତ୍ତିକି and ରାତିକି makes a seasonal observation easy to remember. The line draws attention to night rather than declaring that the whole day has turned cold. In conversation it can accompany noticing a change in the air. This is a calendar-linked saying, not a forecast for every place or year.
meaning_odia: କାର୍ତ୍ତିକି ସହ ରାତିକିର ମିଳ ଋତୁର କଥାକୁ ମନରେ ରଖିଦିଏ। ଧାଡ଼ିଟି ଦିନସାରା ଶୀତର କଥା ନକହି ରାତିର ଥଣ୍ଡାକୁ ଲକ୍ଷ୍ୟ କରେ। ସନ୍ଧ୍ୟା ପରେ ପବନ ବଦଳିଥିବା ଅନୁଭବ କଲେ ଏହି କଥା ମନେ ପଡ଼ିପାରେ। ସବୁ ଜାଗାରେ ସବୁ ବର୍ଷ ଏକା ପାଗ ହେବ ବୋଲି ଏହାକୁ ଧରିବା ନୁହେଁ।
english_summary: A rhyme links Kartika with the chill felt at night.
odia_summary: କାର୍ତ୍ତିକ ଓ ରାତିର ଶୀତକୁ ଶବ୍ଦର ମିଳ ମନେ ରଖାଏ।
usage_example: While sitting outside after sunset in Kartika, someone reaches for a shawl and repeats the line. (Original imagined example, not collected testimony.)
cultural_context: Source identifies Kartiki with Kartika and labels the line Dhaga; it supplies no climate dataset or regional distribution. Distinct from existing Magha sayings.

odia: ଯେ ତବତ ଖାଇଛି ସେ ପଖାଳ ଖାଉ, ଯେ କିଛି ନ ଖାଇଛି ସେ ଗାଧୋଇ ଯାଉ
title: More for the fed, nothing for the hungry
literal_meaning: Let the one who has eaten hot rice have pakhala; let the one who has eaten nothing go off to bathe.
explanation: The people already fed receive another dish, while those who have had nothing are sent away. The dictionary’s figurative sense of going to bathe—being deprived of an enjoyment—makes the exclusion explicit. The pairing sounds almost like an orderly instruction, but the distribution it describes is upside down. It can give a speaker a pointed way to expose favouritism: those already served are served again, and unmet need is dismissed. This is an editorial reading of the contrast, not a rule about who deserves food.
meaning_odia: ଯିଏ ଗରମ ଭାତ ଖାଇସାରିଛି, ତାକୁ ପୁଣି ପଖାଳ; ଯିଏ କିଛି ଖାଇନାହିଁ, ତାକୁ ଗାଧୋଇ ଯିବାକୁ କୁହାଯାଉଛି। ଗାଧୋଇ ଯିବାର ଲକ୍ଷଣାର୍ଥ ଅଭିଧାନରେ କୌଣସି ଲାଭ ବା ଉପଭୋଗରୁ ବଞ୍ଚିତ ହେବା। ଶୁଣିବାକୁ ବଣ୍ଟନର ନିର୍ଦ୍ଦେଶ ଭଳି, ହେଲେ ଭାଗବଣ୍ଟାଟି ପୂରା ଓଲଟା। ଯାହାର ମିଳିସାରିଛି ତାକୁ ଆହୁରି ମିଳୁଛି, ଯାହାର କିଛି ନାହିଁ ତାକୁ ଦୂରେଇ ଦିଆଯାଉଛି—ଏହି ଅନ୍ୟାୟକୁ ଦେଖାଇବାରେ କଥାଟିର କଟାକ୍ଷ ଲାଗିପାରେ। ଏଠାରେ ଆମେ ସେହି ବୈଷମ୍ୟକୁ ଚିହ୍ନଟ କରି ପଢ଼ୁଛୁ, ତାକୁ ଠିକ୍ ବୋଲି କହୁନାହୁଁ।
english_summary: A seemingly orderly instruction exposes an unfair distribution: more for those already served.
odia_summary: ଯାହାର ମିଳିସାରିଛି ତାକୁ ଆହୁରି, ବାକି ଲୋକଙ୍କୁ କିଛି ନାହିଁ—ଏହି ଓଲଟା ବଣ୍ଟନର କଟାକ୍ଷ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: A workshop gives extra notebooks to participants who already received supplies, while late arrivals are told there are none for them. One participant quotes the saying to question the arrangement and asks for the remaining notebooks to be shared fairly.
cultural_context: The hot-rice sense of ତବତ is independently checked in a second entry of the same dictionary lineage (revision221175), not an independent witness to the saying. Pakhala is retained as the food name. Unlike existing166, this is about unequal allocation and exclusion, not deciding between dishes before asking.

odia: ଢିଙ୍କି ପଡ଼େ ଧମଧମ, ସାହାବ ଚାକିରି ଭାରି କଠିଣ; ଝାଳ ବୁହେ ଗମଗମ
title: The sound and sweat of work
literal_meaning: The dheṅki falls thump-thump; service to the sahib is very hard; sweat streams.
explanation: The heavy beat of the pounding implement is answered by the sound of streaming sweat. Between them comes the complaint that service to the sahib is hard. Sound makes the labour felt before any abstract judgment is offered. The line can be read as a rhythmic complaint about demanding work, but the quotation does not identify an employer, worker or event. A present-day speaker may borrow its exaggerated beat to describe a tiring task; that is a new use, not evidence of a particular historical labour arrangement.
meaning_odia: ଢିଙ୍କିର “ଧମଧମ” ଶବ୍ଦ ପରେ ଝାଳର “ଗମଗମ” ଆସୁଛି। ମଝିରେ ସାହାବଙ୍କ ଚାକିରି କେତେ କଠିନ, ସେ ଅଭିଯୋଗ ରହିଛି। ଶବ୍ଦର ତାଳରେ କାମର ଭାର ଓ ଶରୀରର କ୍ଳାନ୍ତି ଏକାଠି ଶୁଣାଯାଏ। ଆଜି କେହି ନିଜର କଠିନ କାମକୁ ନେଇ ଏହା କହିଲେ ପୁରୁଣା ଚିତ୍ରଟି ନୂଆ ପ୍ରସଙ୍ଗକୁ ଆସେ; କିନ୍ତୁ ମୂଳ ପଦର କର୍ମୀ ବା ସାହାବଙ୍କ ପରିଚୟ ଆମ ପାଖରେ ନାହିଁ।
english_summary: Thumping sound and streaming sweat turn a complaint about hard service into a rhythmic line.
odia_summary: ଢିଙ୍କିର ଶବ୍ଦ ଓ ଝାଳର ଚିତ୍ରରେ କଠିନ ଚାକିରିର ଅଭିଯୋଗ ତାଳ ପାଏ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: After repeatedly moving heavy boxes for a demanding organiser, a volunteer recites the line to a friend, tapping out “ଧମଧମ.” The friend hears both the joke and the complaint about the workload.
cultural_context: Source label is Dhaga under an onomatopoeic word. The term sahib is retained as an unspecified form of address/status in the quotation; no colonial employer, date, caste or documented work scene is inferred. Not identical to048 compulsory work wherever one goes.

odia: ଲଙ୍କା— ଗଡୁଁ ଯେତେକ ଜାତ, ସମସ୍ତେ ଅସୁରଙ୍କ ସୁତ
title: One verdict for everyone
literal_meaning: All who are born from Lanka’s fortress are sons of asuras.
explanation: The force falls on “all”: a shared place becomes a single verdict about everyone born there. The dictionary supplies the totalizing word and quotation; its Lanka entry separately identifies the mythological capital. Our critical reading notices how quickly this image shuts out individual differences. It can help us examine a sweeping accusation, but birthplace or descent does not establish anyone’s character.
meaning_odia: କଥାର ଜୋର “ସମସ୍ତେ” ଉପରେ—ଗୋଟିଏ ଜାଗାରେ ଜନ୍ମ ହେଲେ ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କୁ ଏକ ରାୟରେ ବାନ୍ଧିଦିଆଯାଉଛି। ଅଭିଧାନର ଲଙ୍କା ଶବ୍ଦରେ ପୌରାଣିକ ରାଜଧାନୀର ଅର୍ଥ ମଧ୍ୟ ଅଛି। ଆମର ସମାଲୋଚନାତ୍ମକ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ଏହି ଚିତ୍ର ଦେଖାଏ କିପରି ଗୋଷ୍ଠୀର ନାମରେ ବ୍ୟକ୍ତିର ଭିନ୍ନତା ଲୁଚିଯାଏ। ଜନ୍ମସ୍ଥାନ ବା ବଂଶରୁ ମଣିଷର ଚରିତ୍ର ସ୍ଥିର ହୁଏ ବୋଲି ଆମେ ଏହି ରାୟକୁ ଗ୍ରହଣ କରୁନାହୁଁ।
english_summary: Our critical reading questions a single verdict imposed on a whole group.
odia_summary: ଗୋଟିଏ ନାମରେ ସମସ୍ତଙ୍କୁ ଦୋଷୀ ଭାବିବାର ରାୟକୁ ଆମ ପଢ଼ା ପଚାରେ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: After one team member breaks a promise, a friend declares that the whole team is alike. Another quotes the Lanka line and asks whether they have just made the same sweeping judgment. The expression is being examined critically, not endorsed as a rule about the team.
cultural_context: 212713 sense2 is lexical context only. Mythological imagery is not evidence about a present-day population; no event, epic authorship or origin of this saying is established.

odia: ଜର ଅଇଲା ଧାନକୁଟା ବେଳକୁ ଜର ଛାଡ଼ିଲା ଭାତ ଫୁଟା ବେଳକୁ
title: A fever with pointed timing
literal_meaning: Fever came at paddy-pounding time; fever left at rice-boiling time.
explanation: The paired arrivals make the timing conspicuous: illness accompanies one stage of food preparation and disappears at another. Our reading hears a possible teasing suspicion about avoiding the harder work. The source does not prove that anyone pretended to be ill, and boiling rice is not yet eating it. The contrast can carry an accusation without making that accusation true.
meaning_odia: ଖାଦ୍ୟ ପ୍ରସ୍ତୁତିର ଗୋଟିଏ ପର୍ଯ୍ୟାୟରେ ଜର ଆସେ, ଅନ୍ୟ ପର୍ଯ୍ୟାୟରେ ଛାଡ଼େ—ଦୁଇ ସମୟକୁ ଯୋଡ଼ି କଥାଟି ନଜର ଟାଣେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ କଠିନ କାମ ଏଡ଼ାଇବା ପ୍ରତି ଟାହିମିଶା ସନ୍ଦେହ ଶୁଣାଯାଇପାରେ। କେହି ମିଛରେ ଅସୁସ୍ଥ ହୋଇଥିଲେ ବୋଲି ଉତ୍ସ ପ୍ରମାଣ ଦିଏନାହିଁ; ଭାତ ଫୁଟିବା ମଧ୍ୟ ଖାଇବା ନୁହେଁ। ବିରୋଧରେ ଅଭିଯୋଗ ଆସିପାରେ, ତାହା ସତ ହୋଇଯାଏନାହିଁ।
english_summary: Our reading notices suspicious timing without treating it as proof of pretence.
odia_summary: ସମୟର ମେଳରେ ସନ୍ଦେହ ଉଠିପାରେ, ଛଳନାର ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: In a reading discussion, someone quotes the two timings and laughs at the apparent convenience. Another points out that illness can change and asks what the line actually establishes. This imagined exchange separates a joke from evidence about a sick person.
cultural_context: The dictionary defines fever abatement. No medical explanation, diagnosis, work instruction or documented household incident is established; the teasing inference is editorial.
